openings.claim: A manifest-ordered boundary matrix can report an evidence frontier without mistaking timestamp order or missing records for execution history.
openings.delta: Change the ordering dependency from local timestamps to manifest stages; carry equality, inequality and unknown separately in spreadsheet cells linked to record identifiers. Compare only matching artifact boundaries. Report the earliest recorded mismatch, with an unresolved preceding interval wherever evidence cannot exclude an earlier divergence.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, timestamp-first mismatch ranking, the skewed export timestamp will not move export ahead of parse. Missing transform evidence will remain unresolved. Record removal will either widen uncertainty or leave an independently supported result unchanged; it cannot create a new definite stage claim.
openings.probe: Assign matrix review and timestamp-first review to the two disjoint three-pair subsets. Log every manual inspection, stopping at twelve per pair and recording residual uncertainty. Freeze outputs before opening answer sheets. Score sheet-covered cases for boundary containment, unsupported claims and reference validity; then apply the specified record removals and check claim downgrades. Disjoint subsets support a feasibility screen, not a causal superiority estimate.
assumptions: The dictionary and manifest permit identification of comparable artifact boundaries; ambiguous matches stay unknown.
A spreadsheet or script can index supplied fields within sixty minutes; no complete manual reconstruction is promised.

Defeat conditions include ambiguous lineage, uncomparable digests, exhausted inspection capacity or intervals excluding a sheet boundary. These limit informativeness, not permission to invent records.
The additional twenty minutes cover scoring and removal checks; unfinished checks are reported. Answer-sheet coverage is not assumed beyond supplied entries.

assessment: One workflow opening, offered as a bounded probe rather than deployment or demonstrated improvement. Each pair receives a cited stage or interval and a next check: inspect the earliest unresolved boundary record still supplied, or state that resolving it needs an unavailable record.
